On the left, an oxygen/hydroxyl fragment connected to cyclohexyl can be seen; in the middle, oxygen is connected to a carbonyl-related fragment; on the right is a chloro-substituted benzene ring connected to a carboxyacyl group; multiple curved arrows indicate redistribution of electrons from oxygen and carbonyl π-bond positions. Reasoning: According to the arrow-pushing given in the problem to update the bonding relationships, after rearrangement or collapse of the carbonate/chloroformate part, the cyclohexyl oxygen is retained and connected to a chlorine-bearing carbonyl carbon, giving cyclohexyl chloroformate, whose SMILES is O=C(Cl)OC1CCCCC1. The right chlorophenyl acyl fragment exists as a neutral carboxylic acid after electron redistribution, whose SMILES is OC(c2cc(Cl)ccc2)=O. The two products are disconnected molecules, therefore they are connected with a dot.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as an arrow-pushing mechanism containing a cyclohexyl oxygen fragment on the left and a chlorophenyl carboxyl fragment on the right. Apply each curved arrow to update the bonds: collapse the carbonate/chloroformate part so the cyclohexyl oxygen remains attached to a carbonyl carbon bearing Cl, giving cyclohexyl chloroformate, O=C(Cl)OC1CCCCC1. Separately, assign the right-hand chlorophenyl acyl fragment as the neutral carboxylic acid, OC(c2cc(Cl)ccc2)=O. Combine disconnected products with a dot to get O=C(Cl)OC1CCCCC1.OC(c2cc(Cl)ccc2)=O.
